analysis:
The weakest point is that the recorded resolution may be a third option that dodges the dilemma rather than resolving it. truth_mercy_dilemma records that the story forces a choice between an accurate record that wounds and a merciful omission that protects belonging. earned_hope records that hope is available only through a chosen, partial remembrance. The choice_of_maps phase then resolves the choice through that same partial, chosen remembrance. A partial record that is honest about what it cannot restore is easy to read as satisfying both horns at once: it is accurate enough to count as truth and merciful enough to protect belonging. If the reader sees that compromise as available on demand, the dilemma loses its cost, and the hope that follows is earned by an elegant compromise rather than by a loss the story has made irreversible.

The candidate leaves the decisive question open. Its own open questions ask whose memory the final record should preserve, who decides, and whether the Guild's lie is ever defensible as mercy or only as control. The relation dilemma_produces_hope records that the dilemma makes hope conditional on a chosen remembrance, but it does not record who makes the choice. If the surveyor chooses for the city, hope reads as one protagonist's act of mercy. If the city chooses through its records, hope becomes communal and the complicity theme is carried by the community rather than by the investigator. Those two readings produce different endings, and the relation does not yet distinguish them.

A second weakness is that the eliciting condition for hope is recorded as a deliberate record that preserves what matters without claiming completeness. That describes a documentary stance, not an event. The candidate does not record which act in the plot earns hope, so hope risks becoming a tone attached to the final document rather than a consequence of the escalating cost. The emotion target hope is author_declared with role supporting, and the complex emotion hope_through_grief is defined by mourning plus continuing life. Those are recorded intentions; they are not evidence that a reader will feel earned rather than consoled.

The challenge does not show the design is wrong. It shows that the relation is underdetermined on exactly the point the author is most likely to care about: who carries the cost of the final choice.

hypotheses.title: Third-option compromise
hypotheses.description: The partial, honest record may satisfy both horns of the dilemma at once, so the reader experiences a compromise rather than a cost. A stronger version would make the omission itself carry a recorded loss that the final record cannot undo.

hypotheses.title: Agency locus of hope
hypotheses.description: If the surveyor alone chooses the remembrance, hope is one protagonist's mercy; if the city chooses through its records, hope is communal. The recorded open question about who decides is the variable that separates these two endings.

uncertainties: The candidate does not record who makes the choice of remembrance, so the relation cannot yet be assessed for whether hope is individual or communal.
The candidate does not record which plot act earns hope; the eliciting condition describes a documentary stance rather than an event.
Whether a reader would experience the resolution as a compromise or as a cost is not established by any recorded field; this is an interpretation.
